Jack Rutland has moved from Wales to Leicester, and recently became the proud father of a son, Graham John. Mention is made elsewhere of his win in the Army Walking Championship.
The war has produced for the Club yet another champion in Jack Rutland, winner of the first Army Road Walking Championship, at Aldershot, Percy Wright finishing fourth.

The walkers too have had a very good record for the season, Jack Rutland, after his transfer to town and subsequent demobilisation, has been in the front rank, winning most of the Open walks, including our own promotion.
The field for the 3 miles walk was small, but Jack Rutland walked in fine style to overtake all those in front of him, and won easing up in the last lap.

Our star performer for the season has undoubtedly been Jack Rutland who, after starting the season with 4th place in the Highgate Open, rapidly improved and subsequently took individual honours in seven consecutive opens.
All the big Southern "Opens" have fallen to us and Harry Churcher, closely followed by Jack Rutland, has once again proved himself unbeatable over his distances.

As time went on we won many other opens, Harry Churcher taking most of the individual honours with Jack Rutland a close second. As yet unbeaten, our lowest score was in the Cambridge Harriers open, when our placings were 1, 2, 3 and 5.

Harry Churcher, going over the course for the first time, found it necessary to keep with Jack Rutland the greater part of the way. Once again our leading pair, Harry Churcher and Jack Rutland, soon made it clear that they intended showing the rest of the field a pair of clean heels, and although Harry maintained the lead for the best part of the way, Jack succeeded in catching him and they finished together in the fastest time…

Jack Rutland, on returning to the common, then went up into second place, and with McMullen, Joe Coleman, Len Fletcher and Bob Readman not far behind it soon became apparent that, barring a number of accidents, we should add one more to our list of successes.

Although Jack Rutland set a hot pace at the start and gained a lead of about 40 yards, after 2 miles he went slightly off the course. This gave Harry Churcher the chance to catch up with him and after a neck and neck race, Harry eventually took the lead to win by 23 seconds.

For our return match with the Police, although we were without Jack Rutland and Colin Sutton, the police also were not at full strength, the result being that we avenged our defeat earlier in the season.

The very fast course was lengthened by 300 yards so that no comparison can be drawn with previous times, but despite this for the first time since the new handicapping system was introduced, the time standard of 53.30 was broken by Harry Churcher, who completed the course in 53.15, 29 seconds in front of Jack Rutland.

Jack Rutland's performance is particularly worthy of mention, since we had begun to feel that his best distance was 7 miles. A week later the new National Road Champion gained still further honours by annexing once more the A.A.A. title on the track at 7 miles.

Continuing with the 10,000 metres trials which were held during the summer, on 21st July, Harry Churcher led the field at Motspur Park, to put up the very fine time of 46.22.4, with Jack Rutland second in 49.48.
After Jack Rutland had received one of his few disqualifications, our Cadogan team managed to finish 3rd, Enfield beating us into the place by 1 point.

Jack Rutland informs us that he will soon be out training again with an eye to long distance. Jack already holds an important executive post and he is now studying for further promotion.
